# Contribute your site package

**7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage every developer, designer and partner who has built a site
package to submit it by pull request to the repository that holds the package server's contents.** An accepted
package becomes part of Exponential's default distribution system: it is listed in the package index that every
installation reads, so the setup wizard, the kickstarter, `exp:install` and ezupdate on every Exponential site can
offer it, with no extra settings on anyone's side.

This page is for whoever has a working site package (or is about to make one) and wants it to reach every
installation. It answers: which repository to fork, where your files go, what must be in the package, which version
number to give it, which license, how to test it first, what to write in the pull request and how review works.

## Why contribute

- **Reach.** A package in the default index is one click away in every new installation: the setup wizard's
  site package step lists every `type="site"` package of the index
  (`eZStepSiteTypes::retrieveRemotePackagesList()` in `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`), and the kickstarter
  and `exp:install --package=<name>` install it by name.
- **Shared maintenance.** The packages on the server are rebuilt for every Exponential release (one folder per
  release below `exponential/6.0/`: thirteen folders today, from `6.0.0` to `6.0.15`). A package that is part of that set travels with the
  releases instead of aging on one person's disk.
- **Community growth.** Every site package shows what Exponential can do. The Exponential Foundation and 7x want
  many of them: business sites, intranets, portals, shops, community sites, sites in many languages.

You keep your own source repository and your own copyright; the pull request adds the built package and its index
entry to the shared server.

## The repository to fork

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The package server's contents (fork this one) | [github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth) |
| What it publishes | [exponential.packages.exponential.earth](https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/) (GitHub Pages, default branch `master`) |
| The index the 6.0.15 setup wizard reads | [exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml](https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml) |

Every push to `master` publishes the whole tree through the workflow `.github/workflows/workflow.yml`, which also
generates the directory listing you see in a browser ([The package server on GitHub](package-server/the-package-server-on-github.md)).

```bash
gh repo fork se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth --clone
cd exponential.packages.exponential.earth
git checkout -b add-<your_package>
```

The repository is large (it holds every built `.ezpkg` of every release). A partial clone is enough to work in:
`git clone --filter=blob:none <your fork's URL>`.

Keep the **source** of your package (the unpacked folders) in a repository of your own, the way the 7x packages
live in [se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage) and the CJW packages in
[se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage)
([The source repositories](package-server/the-source-repositories.md)). Reviewers will want to see it.

## Folder layout and file names

The server keeps one folder per Exponential release. Your files go into the folder of each release you support,
next to the existing packages:

```text
exponential/6.0/6.0.15/
├── index.xml                          the index: add one <package> line per package
├── <your_package>.ezpkg               the site package (type site)
├── <your_package>_democontent.ezpkg   the packages it requires, if any
└── thumbnails/
    └── <your_package>.png             the picture the setup wizard shows
```

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| File name = `<package name>.ezpkg`, the name exactly as in `<name>` of `package.xml` | The index points at the file, and the importer refuses a name that is not lower case letters, digits and `_` ([Required package.xml fields](requirements/package-xml-required-fields.md)) |
| A name of your own, never one that exists | An import refuses a package whose name is already in any repository of the site ([Packages guide](../../guides/packages.md#6-uploading-a-package)) |
| Thumbnail in `thumbnails/<package name>.png` | The same pattern every existing site package uses (`thumbnail_url` in `index.xml`) |
| Packages your site package requires are on the server too | The wizard downloads every required package from the same index ([Dependencies and the install order](basics/dependencies-and-install-order.md)) |
| Built archives only, no source folders | The server serves files; the source belongs in your own repository |

Build each `.ezpkg` the way the shipped ones are built: a gzip compressed tar of the package folder's contents
(`package.xml` at the top), without `.git`, editor files and `node_modules`
([Rebuilding with build.sh](your-own/rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).

## The index entry

Add your packages to the release's `index.xml`, in the same form as the existing entries. Required packages get a
short entry in the dependency list at the top; the site package gets a full one:

```xml
<package name="<your_package>_democontent" type="contentobject"
         url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/<your_package>_democontent.ezpkg"/>

<package name="<your_package>" version="1.0.0-0" type="site"
         summary="<one line, shown as the package's title>"
         description="<two or three sentences: what the site is and what it contains>"
         url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/<your_package>.ezpkg"
         thumbnail_url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/<your_package>.png"/>
```

The wizard reads every attribute of a `<package>` element as it is, so the URLs must be absolute and correct; it
lists only `type="site"` entries as choices. Check the file with `xmllint --noout index.xml` before you commit
([The index.xml format](package-server/the-index-xml-format.md)).

## The package checklist

The full list, with the reason for each item, is [The requirements checklist](requirements/the-requirements-checklist.md).
In short, before you open the pull request:

- [ ] `package.xml` is well formed, has `<package>` as its root and no document type.
- [ ] `<name>` is lower case letters, digits and `_`, and matches the file name.
- [ ] `<summary>` and `<description>` say what the site is, in plain words.
- [ ] `<vendor>` names you or your organization.
- [ ] `<type value="site" />` for the site package; the right type for each package it requires.
- [ ] `<version>` (`<number>`, `<release>`) agrees with the `version` attribute of the index entry (the `version` attribute of the root `<package>` element is the format version; leave it as the tools write it).
- [ ] `<ezpublish><version>` names the Exponential release you tested with (the element keeps its historical name).
- [ ] `<licence>` holds a license identifier from `package.ini [LicenseSettings]`, and `documents/LICENCE` holds the
      license text.
- [ ] `<changelog>` has an entry for this release.
- [ ] `<maintainers>` lists a maintainer and a role from `[MaintainerSettings] RoleList`.
- [ ] `<dependencies><requires>` lists every package it needs, and each of them is in the pull request or already
      on the server.
- [ ] `files/default/thumbnail/thumbnail.png` and the index thumbnail exist.
- [ ] No secrets: no passwords, keys, tokens or real e-mail addresses in install scripts, settings or content.
- [ ] The package passes **Validate** on its page in **Setup > Packages**
      ([Validating a package before publishing](requirements/validating-a-package-before-publishing.md)).

## Version numbers

- The package's version is `<version><number>` and `<release>` in `package.xml`; the index repeats it in the
  `version` attribute (`1.0.0-0`, `6.0.15-0` in the current index). Keep the two the same
  ([Version numbers](requirements/version-numbers.md)).
- A changed package gets a new version. A folder on the server is a release of Exponential; within it, raise your
  package's version when you replace its file, and say what changed in `<changelog>` and in the pull request.
- If your package is also tagged in your own repository, the project's rule for tags applies there too: a pushed tag
  is never moved ([A pushed tag is permanent](../designers/distribution/a-pushed-tag-is-permanent.md)).

## License

- **Code** (install scripts, templates, settings, extensions inside the package): a license compatible with the GNU
  GPL, because Exponential itself is GPL 2.0 or later. The package wizard's default is `GPL-2.0-or-later`
  (`package.ini [LicenseSettings] DefaultLicense`). See [GPL for theme code](../designers/distribution/gpl-for-theme-code.md).
- **Documentation** that ships with the package (README, guides): the GNU Free Documentation License 1.3, as for
  Exponential's own documentation ([Free documentation](../free-documentation.md),
  [GFDL for theme documentation](../designers/distribution/gfdl-for-theme-documentation.md)).
- **Images and demo content**: only material you have the right to share, with its license stated. Creative Commons
  licenses are in the wizard's list ([Creative Commons for images](../designers/distribution/creative-commons-for-images.md)).

## Test the install in a sandbox first

Never test a site package on a site that holds real content: installing a site package builds a new site.

1. Make a throwaway installation (a fresh clone with its own SQLite database is the quickest,
   [Testing in a sandbox](your-own/testing-in-a-sandbox.md)).
2. Point it at your packages: either import them into its local repository, or set
   `[RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL` in its `settings/override/package.ini.append.php` to a folder that
   serves your copy of the release folder ([Pointing a site at your package server](your-own/pointing-a-site-at-your-package-server.md)).
3. Install with the setup wizard and once more with `./console exp:install --package=<your_package>` (or the
   kickstarter), so both front ends are proven.
4. Check the result: the site, the administration, the editor siteaccess, the roles, a search, an edit and a
   publish. Read `var/log/error.log` of the sandbox.
5. Remove the sandbox when you are done.

## Open the pull request

Push your branch to your fork and open the pull request against `se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth`,
branch `master`:

```bash
git add exponential/6.0/6.0.15/<your_package>*.ezpkg exponential/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/<your_package>.png exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml
git commit -m "Added: <your_package> site package for 6.0.15"
git push origin add-<your_package>
gh pr create -R se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth --base master
```

Write in the pull request:

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| What it is | One paragraph: the kind of site, its siteaccesses and languages, what an editor gets |
| What it contains | The packages, with their types, and the extensions and designs it needs |
| Source | The link to the repository with the unpacked source |
| Tested | The Exponential version, the database(s) and the front ends you installed with (setup wizard, `exp:install`, kickstarter) |
| License | The license of the code, of the documentation and of the images |
| Maintainer | Who answers issues about the package, and where |

Commit messages follow the project's prefixes (`Added:`, `Updated:`, `Removed:`, `Renamed:`), as the existing history
of the repository does.

## How review works

The repository has a README and no contributing guide of its own at the time of writing, so the general GitHub
flow applies: the maintainers of `se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth` review the pull request, may ask
for changes, and merge it when it is ready. Its first pull request (#1, "added ezwebin and plain site to installation
version", 31 December 2023) went in exactly this way. After a merge, the push to `master` republishes the server
and every installation that reads that release's index sees your package.

Questions about a package before you open a pull request are welcome in the project's issue trackers; see
[When something goes wrong](../when-something-goes-wrong.md) for where each tracker is.
